title: 56 Tamil Nadu MLAs Carry Serious Criminal Charges
excerpt: An ADR report on the 2026 Tamil Nadu election finds 54% of new legislators declared criminal cases — 56 of them serious.
body:
Tamil Nadu's freshly elected 17th Assembly carries a troubling distinction: the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and Tamil Nadu Election Watch released a post-election analysis of winner affidavits on May 9, revealing that more than half of all newly chosen legislators face pending criminal charges.

**What the numbers show:**
ADR analysed the self-sworn affidavits of 233 of the 234 winning candidates from the April 23 vote. Out of those 233 winners, 126 — or 54 per cent — have declared criminal cases against themselves. Among them, 56 newly elected MLAs, or 24 per cent of the incoming house, have declared *serious* criminal cases: offences carrying a maximum punishment of five years or more, including murder, attempt to murder, kidnapping, and crimes against women.

**Party-by-party breakdown:**
AIADMK leads the list of winners with serious cases, with 47 of its elected legislators carrying such charges. TVK, the new ruling party of actor-turned-politician Vijay, has 19 of its 107 winning candidates facing serious charges, while DMK accounts for 14 of its 59 winners. ADR defines serious criminal offences as those carrying a maximum punishment of five years or more, non-bailable offences, or cases involving loss to the public exchequer. The wealth picture is equally striking: 193 of the 233 winners, or 83 per cent, are crorepatis, with total declared assets across the new assembly standing at Rs 11,265 crore.

**What to watch:**
With Vijay staking claim to form the government, the courts and the Supreme Court's 2020 directive — which requires parties to justify criminal-record candidacies on merit, not just 'winnability' — will face their next real test as the new cabinet takes shape.
